articleTitle: Machine Learning Approached for Sophisticated Relay to Mitigate Blackouts in Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This research presents an advanced relay selection framework that leverages artificial intelligence to enhance the reliability of power systems. The proposed approach integrates various machine learning (ML) models to identify and select smart relays in real-time, effectively mitigating blackout conditions. Among the models explored, Random Forest framework demonstrated superior performance in dynamic power system environments. The findings reveal that the proposed framework significantly reduces computational complexity compared to exhaustive search strategies, while delivering the highest performance metrics compared to existing methods. Furthermore, the approach achieves near-optimal secrecy performance, offering a robust and efficient solution for modern power systems.

articleTitle: A Study on Deriving the Economic Critical Distance of LFAC Systems for Offshore Wind Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper explores the distance at which Low Frequency AC (LFAC) becomes more cost-effective than High Voltage AC (HVAC) and High Voltage DC (HVDC) for offshore wind farms. A cost analysis for 100–300 MVA capacities, covering both platform and line costs, shows that HVAC is optimal below 30 km, LFAC outperforms HVDC at intermediate ranges, and HVDC becomes economical at longer distances, particularly for higher capacities. Assuming linear scaling for Variable Frequency Transformer (VFT) costs, the study highlights the need for future research to address potential nonlinear cost factors.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Coil Sensors for Position Recognition in Wireless Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: In wireless charging, preventing misalignment is extremely important in terms of power-transfer efficiency and charging time. We propose a wireless-charging system for detecting the receiver's position using a multi-coil sensor. We focused on the fact that a sensor structure with large errors is not practical when recognizing positions using a deep neural network (DNN). To improve the number and placement of sensor coils, the position-recognition errors are evaluated using a DNN. Simulation results show that adding four sensor coils improves the accuracy of position detection compared to two or three, the outer diameter of the sensor coils should not be too large, and the distance from the center of the sensor coil to the center of the receiver coil should be short.

articleTitle: Comparison of Equivalent Circuit Model and LSTM-Based Model for Battery Condition Estimation of Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: To monitor and analyze the state of energy storage batteries, two methods for estimating the state of charge (SoC) are proposed: (1) circuit model-based SoC estimation and (2) machine learning-based SoC estimation. For the circuit model-based method, an equivalent circuit for energy storage battery is modeled using resistors and capacitors, and then an extended Kalman filter is utilized to optimize the battery condition estimation. For machine learning-based method, long short-term memory (LSTM) with historical battery data is used to model battery condition estimation. Both methods show good estimation results. However, LSTM exhibits lower error rates in terms of root mean square error (RMSE). Therefore, for energy storage batteries whose performance cannot be tested, historical data-driven LSTM can more accurately estimate the SoC of the battery.

articleTitle: GaN Power HEMT with Breakdown Voltage >800 V Grown by MBE
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: We report on a GaN power HEMT with a breakdown voltage exceeding 800 V, grown by MBE on sapphire. The high breakdown voltage, surpassing 800 V, is achieved through the use of an ultra-thin AlN buffer layer grown by MBE and the implementation of a single-level gate field plate technique. The MBE technique facilitates the growth of a dopant-free buffer layer and pseudomorphic epilayers, which is advantageous for the high reliability of GaN power HEMTs. Additionally, the single-level gate field plate technique aids in reducing the overall fabrication cost and also enhances the reliability of GaN power HEMTs. These merits highlight the potential of the reported GaN power HEMT for applications in high-power electronics.

articleTitle: Technical and Economic Evaluation of Class F and Class H Insulation in Dry-Type Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Dry-type transformers are integral components in electrical distribution and power systems, providing reliable and efficient energy conversion in various applications. Different insulation classes significantly influence the performance of these transformers. This study compares the F and H insulation classes of dry-type transformers, commonly used in distribution and power systems. These insulation classes differ in terms of performance, cost, and operational characteristics. The analysis focuses on the advantages, economic efficiency, load losses, core losses, and temperature resistance of both classes. The findings show that F-class transformers., which can withstand temperatures up to 155°C and have an average winding temperature rise of 100°C, are cheaper to make and have lower load losses than H-class transformers. This makes F-class transformers particularly suitable for applications prioritizing cost efficiency and reduced energy losses. On the other hand, H-class transformers can handle higher temperatures. They have a maximum temperature resistance of 180°C and an average winding temperature rise of 125°C. This makes them perfect for applications that need to work with high loads for a long time in hot places. The findings indicate significant differences between the two classes in terms of both cost and performance, offering valuable insights for transformer designers to optimize the design.

articleTitle: A Study on the Health Assessment of Sub-Modules in MVDC Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the health assessment of Sub-Modules, which are critical components of MVDC power conversion systems. The focus is on identifying failure modes and their effects through Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), specifically targeting key components such as IGBTs and capacitors. Evaluation criteria are proposed to classify the health condition into five levels based on diagnostic methods. This research aims to lay the groundwork for developing an asset management system that can be applied to the entire DC transmission and distribution system in the future.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis for Oil-Immersed Power Transformers and On-Load Tap Changers Using Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: In power transformers, insulating oil is primarily used to insulate and cool windings and iron cores. When a transformer fails, its high temperature, discharge, and arc phenomenon will cause gas to be generated in the insulating oil. The condition inside the transformer can be analyzed and possible fault types can be diagnosed by analyzing the dissolved gas in the insulating oil. This study proposes a novel method for fault diagnosis based on dissolved gas analysis. The proposed method implements an intelligent fault diagnosis model using an ensemble learning method, which can be used for individual fault assessment of power transformers and on-load tap changers. In the design of the input data of the proposed fault diagnosis model, the percentages of five gases (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CH4, C2H6, C2H4, C2H2) are selected. Finally, the normal and fault data from a power company and IEC TC10 document are used to train the proposed model. Subsequently, actual data from a technology company are used for testing. The test results verify the feasibility of the proposed fault diagnosis technology. The accuracy of transformer fault diagnosis exceeds 71 % (seven diagnostic types) and more than 82 % (three diagnostic types); the accuracy of on-load tap changer fault diagnosis achieves 75 % (three diagnostic types).

articleTitle: Assessments of the Potential for Integrating Battery Energy Storage System into Vietnam National Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The global energy transition is accelerating with the integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) into the power grid, and Vietnam is no exception. However, when integrating RES, the stability and reliability of the grid become issues that need to be handled. Vietnam's grid currently lacks sources that can respond quickly enough to the uncertainty of RES. Therefore, integrating a fast-response system such as Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is worth considering. This research focuses on assessing the impact of installing the BESS on operational costs and reliability through the Loss of Load Probability (LOLP) and Loss of Load Expectation (LOLE) for Vietnamese power system. The Unit Commitment optimization problem model is formulated as a mixed linear integer programming (MILP) model and solved with PyPSA/CPLEX software. The power system's reliability model is also presented. Data were gathered from the operation and parameters of actual generator units in Vietnam's power system. The results indicate that BESS utilization enhances flexibility, optimizes the use of RES, and reduces the need for traditional sources, thus lowering costs and increasing the reliability of the power system. This study is expected to provide valuable information for planning and investment in this field.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Active Magnetic Bearing for Desert Terrain Installed Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper investigates active magnetic bearings (AMBs) as a solution for wind energy systems in desert environments, where abrasive particles, dust, and extreme temperatures challenge conventional bearings. By using magnetic forces to levitate and stabilize rotors without physical contact, AMBs reduce friction, wear, and the need for lubrication, making them ideal for harsh conditions. However, due to AMBs' nonlinear and dynamic complexities, effective control strategies are essential for maintaining rotor stability and precise positioning. To address these challenges, this study introduces a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control approach for AMBs, optimizing rotor stability and performance in fluctuating desert conditions. The PID controller's gains are carefully fine-tuned to adapt the AMB system to varying operational demands, minimizing displacement errors and enhancing response times. A detailed mathematical model of the AMB system is developed, covering its mechanical and electromagnetic behavior. Extensive simulations using MATLAB/Simulink validate the PID controller's effectiveness, showing consistent rotor stabilization despite external disturbances and load variations. This research advances AMB technology, providing a low-maintenance, resilient, and efficient solution for renewable energy generation in extreme environments.

articleTitle: The Impact of High Penetration of Renewable Energy Generation to Locational Marginal Price and Security of Supply: Case Study at Mae Hong Son City Thailand
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: As the dramatically increasing power supply of renewable energy (RE) generation penetrates the distribution network, the security of the supply of the network, such as voltage level, is affected by the uncertain power output. The unstable voltage is caused by the tap of the distribution transformer, which is usually a fixed tap. In addition, the locational marginal price (LMP) depends on the number of power supplies from RE generation. The LMP of the whole local system is not lower, although the selling price of RE generation is lower than that of others, which results from the oversupply of RE generation to the network. The Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA) distribution network in Mae Hon Son City is also affected by the high penetration of renewable energy generation (RE generation). Currently, the proportion of power supply from RE generation is approximately 38% (in May) and 143% (in October) of total power supply to the load. During an oversupply of RE generation, the excess power reverses to PEA transmission network at approximately 8.79 MWh, which results in the security of supply and cost efficiency of distribution network companies such as PEA. The locational marginal price (LMP) in case of high penetration of RE generation is, however, slightly the same price as the non-penetration of RE generation under the Thailand electricity market condition. Therefore, the local generation management and dispatching are consequently considered for local power supply and demand balancing, maintaining the security of supply and reducing power losses and locational marginal price.

articleTitle: Impact of Sloping Lip Wall on the Efficiency of a Duct-Type OWC Device Placed Over an Inclined Foundation
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The present work investigates the optimal hydrodynamic performance of a land-fixed oscillating water column (OWC) device featurng inclined lip walls and bottom foundations. The focus is on enhancing power extraction efficiency over a wide range of frequencies. Utilizing linear water wave theory alongside boundary element method (BEM) numerical techniques, the research analyzes how key structural parameters–such as chamber width, draft ratios, and inclination angles–affect energy transfer and efficiency. The findings reveal that configurations with moderate chamber width and submergence draft ratio lead to improved performance by enhancing wave energy absorption and reducing air loss. Furthermore, a completely inclined bottom profile significantly boosts energy transfer in the short-wave range. In contrast, inclined bottom profiles with moderate draft ratios (approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_{1}/b\approx 1.0$</tex>) and mid-range inclination angles (around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{1}\approx 45^{\circ}$</tex>) deliver a balanced performance across a broad frequency spectrum. Moreover, fine-tuning the turbine damping parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Lambda_{\text{opt}})$</tex> is crucial for aligning with resonance frequencies, ensuring effective energy conversion. These insights are instrumental in advancing the design of OWC devices for real-world coastal and offshore applications, optimizing energy capture and conversion in various wave conditions.

articleTitle: A Study of Impact of Environment Factor on Power System Equipment Partial Discharge Using Multi-Groups Analysis of Variance and Correlation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to propose an acoustic imager to diagnosis partial discharge for electro-mechanical equipment. A high voltage power generator applied to three types of porcelain insulators one is with 10% salt concentration another is with 20% salt concentration and the other is with salt contaminated for laboratory experiments. Taiwan power system field-measurements collect data will comparison with laboratory experiments for evaluation the prediction of diagnosing partial discharge. One-way ANOVA method which statistical analysis includes data mean and standard deviation and statics test will use to test mean difference larger or small, P value will test mean difference significance between relative humidity groups. Correlation analysis is used to test the relevance degree between humidity on the Partial discharge dB data. The research has the following results: 1.The ANOVA method had verified that when humidity is considered as a factor, there is a very significant mean difference in dB data regardless of laboratory experiments or field measurements. It also detected which between groups the mean difference occurs. 2. The mean of laboratory experiments and field measurements in the same humidity groups can be used to evaluate the predictive value of diagnosing partial discharge through the mean error formulation. 3. The correlation analysis results show that the salt concentration had a negative correlation to positive medium correlation with dB data. Field- measurements had a negative correlation to high correlation with dB data.

articleTitle: Optimized Microgrid Implementation Strategy: A Model for Energy and Profit Efficient ESS
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: With the new electrification policies, microgrids will play a key role in the future. This study implements an optimization algorithm for sizing the storage system in an Electric Vehicle (EV) park equipped with PV roofs (2000 kWp) and 40 Charging Stations (CSs), of which 30 are 22 kW and 10 are 120 kW. The model aims to optimize the size of the storage system to ensure an optimal energy balance, maximize the self-consumption of the energy produced, and minimize the cost of buying energy from the grid. The model considers seasonal photovoltaic generation profiles and load scenarios as inputs to simulate system behaviour realistically. The approach complements the prioritized management of available power to the CSs with an economic analysis of the storage system. The results show how the tradeoff between investment costs, reduction of energy deficits, and revenues from the sale of surplus energy determines the optimal storage capacity. The model is first simulated in island mode, simulating worst-case conditions, to identify the ideal capacity of 850 kWh, then the maximum profitability under normal conditions is tested, which results in 52.39 k€ earned in 10 years. The proposed framework offers a versatile solution to improve the economic and energy sustainability of EV charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic Analysis of Multi-Chamber Oscillating Water Column Device Using RANS Model
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study examines the hydrodynamic performance of multi-chamber Oscillating Water Column (OWC) devices using ANSYS 2022 R1 software, addressing gaps in existing wave energy research. While wave energy offers significant potential for sustainable power generation, most prior studies have focused on single-chamber OWCs or linear wave models, which do not capture the complexities of real-world ocean conditions. The study utilizes the Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) model with the SST <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k-\omega$</tex> turbulence model and the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method to analyze the performance of multi-chamber OWC devices. The analysis focuses on key parameters such as free surface elevation, velocity, and vorticity, offering insights into energy transfer, dissipation, and the effects of turbulent flow on power generation efficiency. The results highlight the importance of chamber interactions and vorticity in influencing energy losses and overall performance. The study finds that multi-chamber systems significantly improve energy capture, with the four-chamber configuration achieving the highest efficiency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\eta=0.23)$</tex> and power output. These findings emphasize the need for optimizing chamber design to minimize energy losses and enhance system performance, particularly under nonlinear wave conditions, and contribute to advancing OWC device optimization and wave energy technology.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Effect of the Uncertainty Parameters on the Technical Virtual Power Plant's Optimal Operating Schedule
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: N owadays, due to the strong integration of renewable energy sources (RES) into distributed grids, Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) have been motivated and have gained significant attention. A concept of VPP is the Technical Virtual Power Plant (TVPP), which considers both commercial and technical aspects when participating in the electricity market. When considering a TVPP, the objective is to optimize profit when participating in the day-ahead (DA) market while ensuring compliance with the technical constraints of the power grid. However, it is difficult to achieve both requirements due to the uncertainty and unpredictability of the RES power output. This paper analyzes the effects of the uncertainty parameters, in this case, the photovoltaic (PV) power output, on the TVPP's operation schedule. Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization Model (TSSOM) and Two-Stage Chance - Constrained Optimization Model (TSCCOM) are applied to determine the optimal scheduling of a TVPP, including PVs, energy storage systems (ESS), and local loads. The TVPP's network is assumed to be the IEEE 15-bus test system. This paper solves the optimization models using GAMS and CPLEX. The results present that when the input of the optimization problem is uncertain, using the TSCCOM optimization program for scheduling operation problems of a TVPP gains better results in maximizing profits while ensuring compliance with technical constraints.

articleTitle: Design and Develop a Feasibility Economics Program for the Optimal Sizing of Photovoltaic Rooftop Installation via Using Google Worksheet
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: In the present day, renewable energy has gained significant popularity worldwide, particularly in rooftop photovoltaic systems in Asia, such as Thailand and Japan. This surge in popularity is mainly due to the accessibility of these systems, which current technologies have dramatically enhanced. These technologies have also urged the growth of photovoltaic design programs. Because the sellers and installers of photovoltaic systems are now required to estimate the solar power available on the rooftop of a building and in a specific area, including the typical investment cost and technical engineering report such as engineering calculation sheets and installation drawings. These can be seen in the various photovoltaic design software such as PVSyst, PV*Sol, RETScreen, SolarEdge, Helioscope, etc. This research aims to design and develop a program using the Google Worksheet to maximize the effectiveness of installation and minimize the investment. The program will be involved in determining the optimal sizing of rooftop photovoltaic systems, assessing the feasibility of the project, and presenting typical installation drawings. The standards and regulations are strictly followed to ensure the safety of installation and the operating system. The proposed program can enable the simulated scenarios based on the electricity provider and electricity tariff to determine the generated energy and forecast potential investment and savings. The program function can support updating materials, data, and pricing using Google Worksheets. The program can also develop the relationship between the engineer, installer, and client as it can present the accuracy and efficiency of the design project and reduce the losses of materials from installation. This makes it an essential program for the engineering, installer and client. The program results are validated against the electricity provider's website and commercial photovoltaic design software such as PVSyst and PV*Sol to ensure performance and accuracy.

articleTitle: Frequency Control in the Islanded Smart Microgrid Via Diesel-Engine Generator
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Diesel-engine generators are employed in power systems for both generating power and energy. In the islanded microgrid, the most important duty for the engine generator is the frequency management. Smart microgrids (SMGs) provide with high-tech controls to solve more rising problems in smart grids. For possessing a reliable and stable SMG, it is important to incorporating an adaptive primary frequency controller for the islanded condition. This duty is hard due to obscure incident of unsure disturbances, loads. We insist novel Diesel-engine generator's frequency control for islanded SMG. The suggested method is according to reinforcement learning control using continual Q-learning. The goal of this paper is to show Q-learning approach for continual systems which figure out the LQR problem without having any knowledge of the system dynamics. Simulation results show effectiveness of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Impulse Polarity Effect on Soil-Enhancement Material Mixtures
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper aims to study the breakdown characteristics of enhancement materials mixtures under both positive and negative impulse polarities. Sand is considered where it is mixed with 5% and 10% of water content, and mixed with several percentage of enhancement material (EM), filled in a parallel plate test cell and subjected under both impulse polarities. Results are analysed at both pre-breakdown and breakdown levels, where impulse impedance, Zimp, breakdown electric field, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> and v-t breakdown curves were compared for both impulse polarities. From the obtained results, it is found that the Zimp, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> and time to breakdown are improved with the presence of EM. Higher Zimp was seen in positive impulse than those obtained for negative impulse polarity. The established data obtained from this work will not only be helpful in understanding the breakdown mechanism of soil-EM mixtures under both impulse polarities, but also it can be considered in representing the equivalent circuit of grounding systems correctly in the simulation work.

articleTitle: A Study on Optimizing Investment Value of Power Transformers Using Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: We are studying a risk-based asset management system for objective decision-making. In order to build an AMS, we must go through the APM and AIPM stages. In order to accurately verify the investment plan established based on risk, we must perform the AIPM stage using an appropriate optimization algorithm. However, the existing linear optimization technique does not consider many constraints and nonlinearity of PoF that must be considered in the process of establishing an investment plan for power facilities. Therefore, we must reflect the AIPM stage appropriately by optimizing using an optimization technique that considers many constraints and nonlinearity of PoF. Therefore, to solve this problem, in this paper, we propose a method to perform the AIPM stage by applying the DDQN (Double Deep Q-Network) method, a reinforcement learning algorithm that can accommodate various constraints and nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Power Purchase Agreements in Sustainable Management for Firm and Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Considering ESG and CSR perspectives, firms are increasingly expected to adopt renewable energy, bringing attention to Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). This study aims to construct a new theoretical PPA model using real options theory to determine the optimal contract timing and the negotiated price in PPA between generation company and firm.

articleTitle: Exploring Values and Perceptions of Renewable Energy in Taiwan from an Environmental Perspective: A Case Study on Geothermal Power
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This research explores Taiwan's renewable energy initiatives through geo-thermal power, integrating the Value-Belief-Norms (VBN) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), alongside political trust and environmental risk. Using the Contingent Valuation Method (CVM), we assessed the ecological compensation that individuals are willing to offer for conservation and geothermal projects. Of the 453 questionnaires distributed, 412 valid responses were obtained, reflecting a response rate of 90.9 %. The study reveals that altruistic and biospheric values significantly influence environmental concerns, supporting VBN theory. Additionally, environmental attitudes and perceived behav-ioral control positively affected intentions toward green energy, promoting pro-environmental actions. Notably, environmental risk moderated the relationship between subjective norms and green energy intentions, indicating that it can influence public acceptance. The willingness to pay (WTP) for a protection fund post-geothermal construction decreased from NT$1,262.2 to NT$1,133.5 per year. These findings emphasize the importance of public opin-ion in shaping sustainable energy policies in Taiwan.

articleTitle: A Method for Calculating the Angle of Attack Applicable to the Rotational Speed Range of Tip Speed Ratio Less Than 1 in a Turbine Performance Analysis Model Using Aerodynamic Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The method of analyzing the performance of vertical axis turbines using aerodynamic performance prediction models, such as multiple streamtube models and double-multiple streamtube models, is widely utilized. These models rely on the aerodynamic characteristics of the blades and require calculating the angle of attack at each moment, based on the relative velocity determined by the prescribed flow speed and the turbine's rotational speed. This study shows that the conventional method for calculating the angle of attack is not applicable to the tip speed ratio is 1 or less. Therefore, this paper proposes a new method for calculating the angle of attack suitable for the tip speed ratios less than 1.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Electronic Nose for Detecting NPK Nutrients of Chicken Manure
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study focuses on the use of an electronic nose device to monitor the NPK nutrients of chicken manure. With the integration of IoT (internet of things), the data gathered through the e-nose is sent through a mobile application created using Arduino Cloud and Arduino IoT Remote application. The system is composed of multiple sensors such as NPK sensor, moisture sensor, temperature, and humidity sensor in which is used to gather the data significant to the study. The researchers propose the use of such system to aid the user in determining whether the chicken manure is ready to be used or not by observing its nutrient content.

articleTitle: Virtual Inertia Compound Control Strategy for Interconnection System with Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Variable inertia presents a potential alternative method for improving transient stability in power systems, due to the increased penetration of new types of generators that have more controllable inertial response, such as wind generators. This paper investigates a novel control strategy of interconnected power grids to improve transient angle stability by coordinating with the variable inertia of regional networks of wind turbines. Based on the dynamic model derived from a two-area, interconnected power system, the impact of controlled inertia on a generator's rotor-angle swing is evaluated theoretically. As a new variable parameter in operation, the proposed scheme not only keeps the controlled inertia's original function of providing rapid frequency response, but also utilizes it to prevent large rotor-angle swing. A two-area power system containing four synchronous generators and two doubly-fed-induction-generator-based wind farms with a high 30% wind penetration is simulated to validate the proposed control strategies. The simulation results show that utilizing wind-power generation to control inertia in the system can reduce power angular deviation following transient events for a significant level of dynamic support, thus greatly reducing the burden of maintaining system transient stability on synchronous generators.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis for Designing Renewable Energy Systems in El-Fasher City, Sudan
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper investigates the techno-economic analysis process for designing renewable energy systems for El-Fasher City, Sudan. First, a solar photovoltaic system for residential use in El-Fasher City is designed using the System Advisor Model (SAM), a robust tool for analyzing renewable energy projects. The study then explores the application of SAM in designing a community-scale wind turbine system at the same site. While the combination of wind power and solar photovoltaics has the potential to enhance the community's sustainability and resilience by creating a more diverse and reliable renewable energy mix, this study analyzes both systems separately. The findings contribute to the development of sustainable energy practices by providing a systematic approach to planning renewable energy systems tailored to specific locations. The results aim to educate policymakers, academics, and practitioners, encouraging the adoption of efficient and effective renewable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Transient Islanding Constrained Resilient Planning of Distribution System to Achieve Secure MG Formation
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Power distribution system is vulnerable to natural disasters, when natural disasters occur, its resilience can be improved by formation of MGs. However, unsafe unplanned islands may trigger cascade shedding of DGs, leading to the failure of forming MG. Therefore, a new resilient investment planning method for distribution systems is proposed in this paper, which not only considers the static safe operation constraints before and after random accidents, but also incorporates the transient island safety constraints. The problem is formulated as a two-stage stochastic programming model with transient constraints. Since the problem cannot be solved directly, a simulation-assisted artificial intelligence method is proposed, in which frequency response simulation under stochastic interrupt of distribution system is built, and an extreme learning machine-based method is used to extract the relationship between the interrupted line power and the lowest frequency of the formed MG. Then it is embedded into the optimization problem. The proposed model and method are verified by a 37-node distribution system to demonstrate its superiority.

articleTitle: Impulse Breakdown Characteristics of Soil-Enhancement Material Mixtures
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper presents and analyses the results of soil mixed with controlled amount of enhancement material (EM) and water content (WC) filled in a parallel plate test cell, subjected to high impulse currents. Up-and-down tests are carried out to determine the breakdown voltage, U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50,</inf> which gives the corresponding electric field, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> of a range of soil mixtures. From the obtained results, it is found that the impulse impedance, Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">imp</inf>, measured at pre-breakdown level decreases with percentage of EM and WC. E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> and time to breakdown, t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> are lower in soil-EM mixtures than that obtained in soil without EM.

articleTitle: Parameters Optimization of Oyster Wave Energy Converter Devices Using Artificial Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: A supervised machine learning model based on artificial neural network (ANN) is used for the optimization of various parameters of an Oyster device. Oyster is a surface-piercing flap type device which works in nearshore environment and extracts energy by pitching about a horizontal axis parallel to the seabed. In this study, the shape parameters associated with the Oyster's flap and foundation will be taken as input parameters to the ANN model and the efficiency of the Oyster device will be considered as output parameter. Initially, the problem will be solved using 3D boundary Element Method. For the training and testing database, Latin Hypercube Sampling technique will be used to obtain highly stratified input samples. The developed ANN model will be used to generate a large dataset consisting of combinations of various input parameters and associated output parameter. These large datasets will be used for the optimization purpose to achieve maximum efficiency from the Oyster device.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Frequency-Based Security Constrained Unit Commitment
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study investigates the capability of an offline reinforcement learning-based approach to address the dual objectives of optimal generation operation and system frequency stability. The Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is used to produce generator status, initial voltage magnitude, active power generation, and reactive power generation for a given load profile and distribution. The New England 39-bus model is used as the the test case. This study generates 2,116 random scenarios and operating points with N-1 contingencies. The research findings indicate that the generator capacity utilization factor impacts frequency stability. The DDPG algorithm is able to understand the characteristics that lead to its capability in providing actions towards better stability and lower operational costs. In offline training with tabular data, DDPG achieves average rewards of 0.237, higher than random actions at 0.079.

articleTitle: Predictive Charging Management for Battery Swapping Stations of Electric Scooters in Busan
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Electric scooters (ESs) offer a sustainable alternative to urban logistics but face challenges such as limited range and long charging times. Battery swapping station (BSS) addresses these issues by enabling quick battery exchanges, reducing operational downtime and improving efficiency. Unlike conventional BSS, this study specifically focuses on BSSs of ESs, which show different usage behaviors from large electric vehicles and pose distinct operational challenges due to their smaller battery capacities and higher frequency of exchanges. This study proposes a predictive charging management algorithm designed for multiple BSSs of ESs. By predicting hourly demand and dynamically controlling fast and slow charging, the algorithm minimizes unnecessary fast charging, ensuring efficient resource utilization while maintaining battery availability. Simulation using a digital twin model demonstrated the delivery of resource-and cost-efficient battery exchange solutions while satisfying ES riders with predictive charging management algorithm. These findings underscore the algorithm's adaptability to optimize energy consumption and resource allocation, paving the way for its integration into smart city infrastructures.

articleTitle: Use of Syngas Produced from Coconut Shells Fueled for a Petrol Engine Generator
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Naturally burned coconut shells cause air pollution and contribute to global warming. They can be converted into syngas to be used as an alternative fuel. Thus, this research aims to study the performance and pollutant of a petrol engine generator using syngas and its mixtures at 1,500 rpm and different loads. Syngas was generated from coconut shells by a medium-sized downdraft gasifier. The syngas flow was increased from 13 to 27 kg/hr. The best load using 100% syngas was found at 60% by adjusting the ignition timing at 25o BTDC using a modified compression ratio of 10:1. Electrical power was reduced by only 16.64%, and engine performance was slightly lower than gasohol 91. Pollutants, such as carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and unburned hydrocarbon, from using 100% syngas were lower than those using gasohol 91. Additionally, the dual-fuel gasohol 91 combined with syngas and air flows at 13 kg/hr increased engine performance and decreased carbon dioxide better than gasohol91.

articleTitle: Optimal Formation of Energy Communities Under Technical-Spatial Constraints
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The growing incorporation of renewable energy sources, electric vehicles, and energy storage systems within modern power systems has amplified the need for efficient energy management frameworks. This paper presents a novel optimization approach for clustering prosumers into energy community groups to enhance self-sufficiency, operational efficiency, and economic performance. The proposed framework incorporates an initial number of prosumers with energy assets, including photovoltaic systems, storage, and electric vehicles, aiming to form energy communities while addressing the distribution grid's technical and physical constraints. The optimization problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming model, capturing the nonlinear relationships and discrete decision variables involved in prosumer clustering, complying with grid operational limits, and minimizing power losses within the distribution network. The optimization outcomes demonstrate significant improvements in energy utilization, reducing grid dependency and cost savings for prosumers, enabling greater economic and technical benefits. The results indicate a 43.4 percent reduction in the energy bills of prosumers following their participation in the energy community. This study provides policymakers and grid operators a tool to cluster prosumers by considering technical and regulatory constraints.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimized Adjustment Method for Medium-Long Term Contract of Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The optimized adjustment of medium-long term contract curves is very important for the electricity market development. One optimization method considering typical rules of China's electricity market is proposed in this paper. The method focus on the medium-long term contract power curve last chance to adjust before the day-ahead spot market, new emerging market entities with energy storage or load regulation capabilities are taken as the sides of the contract. Firstly, the optimized adjustment strategies is provided, and based on the price difference contract mechanism between with the medium-long term and spot markets, the optimization model is formed with the goal of maximizing the overall profits of both sides. To reduce the impact of load and electricity price uncertainty, one data-driven based DRO (Distributionally Robust Optimization) algorithm is adopted. After the optimization of contract, one transferring benefits and power relocation cost allocation method is proposed by applying the Shapley allocation algorithm, makes both sides of the contract can autonomously negotiate by common accepted rules. Case study shows that the method can reduce the risk of price fluctuations in the spot market, improve the overall economic level of medium-long term contract, and make better connection between with the medium-long term market and the spot market.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Planar Flyback Transformer for Isolated Power Supply Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The conventional wire wound magnetic components have exposed several limitations in terms of high power density, high operating frequency, and low profile in DC-DC power converters. The planar magnetic has eliminated the limitations of conventional transformers. Planar transformers are perfect for limited space applications since they are often smaller and flatter than wire-wound transformers where wire wound transformers are bulky. This project involved a reduction in height of 50% from a conventional wire-wound transformer while achieving comparable electrical performance. In low-power DC-DC converter applications, flyback topology is often used as it is simple in structure and provides better isolation. In this project, a 2.5W flyback converter is designed with a planar transformer. The design of the planar transformer was accomplished by using Ansys PEmag. According to the PEmag simulation design, the PCB was designed in Altium Designer. Then, it was exported to a finite element analysis-based software, Ansys Maxwell 3D, for further analysis including leakage inductance & coupling coefficient. A multi-physics circuit simulator, Ansys Simplorer, was also introduced in this project to observe the overall performance of the flyback converter with the designed planar transformer.

articleTitle: Study of Sinusoidal Switching Angle-Based Asymmetrical Multilevel Solar Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Multilevel inverters are well recognized for producing high-quality switched waveforms with reduced harmonic distortion compared to other conventional inverters. Their ability is to generate more accurate output waveforms at lower switching frequencies without distortion and has led to increased interest in recent years. In this paper, a review of a commonly used multilevel inverter scenario is conducted, with a focus on the impact of sinusoidal switching angle-based on total harmonic distortion (THD). From the three primary topologies-diode-clamped, flying capacitor-clamped, and cascaded H -bridge, the cascaded H-bridge was selected due to its requirement for fewer components and benefits. An asymmetric configuration was chosen for the analysis, with both experimental and simulation studies conducted on output voltages up to seven levels using PSIM software. Proper switching angles were maintained throughout the study. The research demonstrates that higher-level multilevel inverters can be produced using fewer H-bridge cells while reducing harmonic distortion. Experimental results validate the simulation results, confirming the importance of the mentioned system.

articleTitle: Portable Off-Grid Solar Power Generation System for Emergency Energy Supply
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: In remote areas and areas not covered by conventional power grids, access to stable electrical energy is a major challenge. Limited infrastructure and the high cost of electricity supply make alternative renewable energy sources, such as solar power, a promising option. However, the implementation of flexible and portable solar power systems for small-scale needs in these areas is still limited. Therefore, this study aims to design and develop a portable solar power generation system that can meet small-scale energy needs in off-grid locations. The system consists of a 120 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{p}}$</tex> photovoltaic (PV) module, a 10A solar charging regulator, a 12V 100Ah VRLA battery, and a 1200 W inverter, all of which are housed in a compact panel box with a metal base equipped with wheels for high mobility. Based on energy analysis, the system proved to be capable of meeting the daily energy demand of 0.1755 kWh. Performance tests show that the system can provide stable power despite fluctuating weather conditions. Effective management of the energy storage enables continuity of power supply despite a decrease in sunlight intensity. Nonetheless, there is potential to improve the energy conversion efficiency by adjusting the solar panel angle and adding PV capacity. This portable solar power system offers a sustainable, flexible, and practical solution to meet the energy needs of the community.

articleTitle: Establishing a Certification System for the Field Project of Outdoor Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Taiwan actively promotes energy transformation and net zero emissions. Generating 15.1% of energy using renewable sources by 2025 and reducing net zero emissions by 2050 is a goal set by Taiwan. Solar, Wind, and other renewable energy sources will be built on a large scale. The intermittent supply features of renewable energy will affect the traditional power grid. An energy storage system is a key technology to reduce the influence of intermittent renewable energy on the power grid, it can solve the problem of integrating renewable energy with the power grid on a large scale. Currently, the technological development of energy storage systems shows a diverse trend. In Taiwan, an energy storage system with a lithium battery is the first choice for most enterprises. Therefore, a certification system for outdoor battery energy storage system field project is proposed in this research for the outdoor grid-integrated energy storage system. This certification system adopts a three-stage certification method, including a design review before construction, field certification after completion, and regular test every two years. It guarantees the safety of the energy storage system and its related equipment. It facilitates the energy storage system industry's development and renewable energy policies.

articleTitle: Development of an Optimization Algorithm for Interconnected Multi-Energy Systems Across Regions for Energy Independence
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Korea faces an energy imbalance due to the concentration of energy demand in the Seoul metropolitan area and the concentration of renewable energy resources in regional areas. To mitigate this issue, the Korean government has developed the 10th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand and the 2050 Carbon Neutrality Scenario, aiming to achieve regional energy autonomy and sustainable energy transitions. The Multi-Energy System (MES), which integrates various energy sources such as electricity, heat, and hydrogen, is essential for addressing the grid instability caused by the increased penetration of renewable energy. Furthermore, MES plays a critical role in realizing regional energy autonomy. This paper proposes the development of an optimization algorithm to enhance regional energy autonomy and optimize inter-regional energy integration through MES. This approach is expected to enhance the stability of Korea's energy supply and provide solutions for achieving carbon neutrality.

articleTitle: Multilevel Inverter Using Nearest-Sine-Level Stage-Capacitors with Coupled and Reduced Number of Power Semiconductor Switches
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper has presented a multilevel inverter (MLI) with reduced number of power semiconductor switches. The MLI is derived from the neutral point clamped (NPC) inverter, where the number of switches at each inverter's upper-part string is reduced and coupled (coupled and reduced number of switches) while still maintaining its performance and functionality. Therefore, the proposed inverter topology is called MLI with coupled and reduced number of switch (CRNS). In order to reduce the total harmonic distortion (THD), the stage-capacitor value for each step/level is set to the nearest-level of sine-wave signal. Compared to a uniform stage-capacitor values (USC) method, the nearest-sine-level stage-capacitor values (NSLSC) show better performance in term of THD and output power. For a 9-level circuit configuration, the THD of the NSLSC method is around 11.97%, and the USC give 14.32% of THD for a certain load setting. The THD can be reduced further by using higher number of levels, with only additional one power switch, one capacitor and one diode for each additional inverter's output level. Another interesting feature of the concept is logic block circuit to implement digital gating signal is also simpler than the conventional method.

articleTitle: Power System Operation as a Viable Island: The Australian Experience
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Regional power balancing is an important require-ment for Australia's National Electricity Market (NEM), which is comprised of an electrical grid interconnecting five regions on the east coast of Australia. In recent years, the NEM has faced significant challenges related to extreme weather events, which have caused failures in power transmission infrastructure-leading to the separation of regional frequencies and the emergence of 'power islands' within the NEM. Consequently, we are motivated to investigate the operation of a regional power system when it is at credible risk of islanding or when it is an island. In this paper, we discuss how South Australia can operate electrically islanded from the rest of the NEM, while confirming to the system strength and inertia requirements. Alternatively, it may be possible to disaggregate power system regions within a connected grid into multiple synchronous zones, each with its own independent frequency and frequency control, thereby making it easier to provide essential services and help prevent widespread blackouts.

articleTitle: Effect of Ambient Temperature Variations on the Design and Performance of Dry-Type Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study investigated the design and performance of dry-type transformers under various average maximum ambient temperatures. The IEC 60076–11 standard was used to model three transformers with different ambient temperatures. Each transformer had the same primary and secondary voltage levels and a power capacity of 2000 kVA. The aim of the study was to determine the effects of changes in ambient temperature on transformer design and to highlight the structural and design differences that occur as a result of temperature variations. Three different transformer models, designed with the same power, voltage, and insulation class (for ambient temperatures of +40°C, +50°C, and +60°C), were compared, and the effects of increasing ambient temperature on the design parameters were investigated. Based on the results obtained, the changes in weight, cost, and loss values of the transformers were analyzed in detail. The study shows important results about how changing ambient temperatures affect the design of dry-type transformers. It also lists the design factors that should be taken into account for managing the performance of these devices effectively in engineering settings.

articleTitle: Design of a Bidirectional Triple Full-Bridge CLLC Converter with Dual-Output Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The DC-DC converters find widespread use across various fields, including automotive systems, battery chargers, and LED driver circuits. For powertrain systems of electric vehicles, the isolated bidirectional topologies are commonly preferred due to their merits. This paper proposes an isolated bidirectional triple CLLC converter to achieve galvanic isolation, bidirectional power flow, and high efficiency. This topology is obtained by integrating three bidirectional CLLC converters, which is particularly well-suited for applications demanding compact design and high efficiency. Integrating three CLLC converters reduces circuit size and hardware cost while enabling multi-directional power flow. In this paper, a prototype CLLC converter with 1 kW rated output power is introduced, featuring six directions of power transmission. Moreover, the effectiveness and performance of the proposed topology are verified by using PLECS simulation software.

articleTitle: Model Based Travelling Wave Fault Location in a Treelike Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The paper studies model algorithms for multi-terminal travelling wave fault location in electrical branched networks. The model algorithm is based on finding the minimum of the loss function when varying the fault location, travelling wave's speed, and line's length. Travelling wave fault location complex calculates the time delay of traveling wave's arrival at each end of the line relative to the base end. Loss function consists of module or modules' sum of calculated and measured time delays' difference. Paper shows that loss function's minimum, considering only two ends of the line, matches the set of combinations of fault location and traveling wave propagation speed. Considering three ends of the line removes the uncertainty associated with the travelling wave propagation speed. If we are to consider all ends of the line we can achieve a reduction of network's length determination error.

articleTitle: Parametric Study of the Compressed Air Energy Storage System and Analysis of Financial Feasibility
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study analyzes the performance and financial feasibility of a compressed air energy storage (CAES) system in Miaoli County, utilizing the underground aquifer. It consists of three parts. First, the system's performance was analyzed using Flownex software, building and validating a model based on the Huntorf case in Germany, which showed about 1% deviation in efficiency. Following this, the output power was adjusted to 2 MW for initial development. The second part involved analyzing geological characteristics using COMSOL software to establish a multiphase flow model, evaluating the flow rate and pressure needed for the CAES system. Finally, a financial analysis estimated component costs and assessed the levelized cost of the proposed CAES system, comparing it to other energy storage technologies to evaluate its financial feasibility. While the investigated designs for the target region in this study have potential for further enhancement, the analysis framework established can be applied in future evaluations of potential areas and financial viability, supporting the process of decision-making.

articleTitle: Electric Circuit Topology Design with Bandwidth Consideration in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the characteristics of wireless power transfer across various applications and analyzes the suitability of resonant circuit topologies for each application domain. It proceeds with impedance matching by employing fundamental concepts of resonant circuits and equivalent impedance calculation formulas specific to each topology. Additionally, it describes the general features of SS and SP topologies. Finally, the paper assesses the appropriateness of these topologies through circuit simulation-bandwidth analysis, using case studies such as wireless electric vehicle charging and wireless power transfer for implantable medical devices.

articleTitle: Dual Closed-Loop Inverter Control System Based on Quasi-PR and PI
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: At present, photovoltaic power generation has been appreciated by all countries, and the inverter, as an equipment to convert direct current into alternating current, is an important equipment to convert solar energy into electricity. Scholars at home and abroad for inverter control strategy do a lot of research, but with the increase of photovoltaic installed capacity and permeability, the accuracy of the inverter output voltage waveform put forward higher requirements, before many control strategy has been unable to meet the requirements, in order to reduce the inverter output voltage distortion rate, this study puts forward a quasi-PR(Proportional Resonant) control and PI(Proportional Integral) control combined double closed-loop control strategy, finally simulation verified the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Prediction of Sequence Impedance for Grid-Connected VSC Based on Interpolation Method
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Renewable energy sources make extensive use of voltage source converters (VSC) for power transfer, and impedance-based schemes provide technical support for their stability analysis. However, due to the difficulty of obtaining the internal parameters of converters in industrial applications, impedance measurements can only be realized by scanning frequency schemes. The implementation of this method is complicated and further hinders by the limited availability of measurement data. Meanwhile, the sequential impedance has a clearer physical interpretation than dq impedance, and it avoids phase coupling. In this paper, a cubic spline interpolation-based sequential impedance identification scheme is proposed for grid-connected VSCs, which can predict the sequence impedance model of the converter at different operating points based on a small amount of frequency scanning data. The proposed scheme does not require training and the prediction is fast. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Transformer Reliability Through Real-Time Machine Learning Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Power transformers are key assets in oil and gas processing facility, and their failure may lead to asset damage, and safety issues. One of the most cost-efficient, easy, and practical transformers monitoring approach in the market is deploying Artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance transformer data and avoid failure. AI can analyze data from various sources, such as Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA), bushing monitoring systems, temperature monitoring systems, and thermal cameras, to predict and prevent power transformer failures. This proactive approach minimizes the risk of unplanned outages and enhances operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Emissions-Aware Energy Storage Decision Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning model to optimize energy arbitrage in energy storage systems while considering real-time electricity prices and carbon emissions. The DRL model uses a deep Q-network algorithm to learn optimal charging/discharging decisions based on historical price and carbon data, aiming to maximize profit and minimize emissions. The model's reward function includes both financial rewards and carbon costs, providing a comprehensive assessment of the impacts of carbon costs on system profitability. The study compares two sets of rewards: one without carbon cost and one with carbon emissions factored in. Results show that carbon costs significantly influence profitability and decision-making strategies. The DRL model adapts by charging less and discharging more during high demand to minimize carbon costs and maximize rewards. The research concludes that with an optimized strategy, it is possible to achieve carbon neutrality while maximizing profit in ESS operations.

articleTitle: Impact of Hydrogen Storage and Flexible Load Management on Grid Emission Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study explores strategies for emission reduction in power systems by integrating hydrogen storage technologies and flexible load management to achieve a sustainable and low-carbon energy future. Hydrogen, as a versatile and clean energy carrier, offers significant potential for decarbonizing energy systems, particularly when paired with renewable energy sources. Flexible load management complements this by balancing supply and demand, improving resource utilization, and ensuring grid stability. The research proposes a mixed-integer programming model to co-optimize hydrogen and electrical energy resources, addressing the challenges of integrating distributed generation, hydrogen technologies, and flexible loads into modern power systems. Additionally, the study focuses on simulating load flexibility and the operational role of green hydrogen to enhance the efficiency of integrated network operations. Applied to the IEEE 39-bus test system, the proposed framework demonstrates its feasibility and effectiveness in minimizing emissions, reducing operational costs, and enhancing system flexibility. These findings provide valuable insights into integrating hydrogen-based systems and flexible load management as key components of future sustainable energy systems.

articleTitle: Big-Data Modeling Based Simscape Power Systems-ST for Protective Relaying
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper introduces novel methodologies for generating Big Data using specialized technology libraries (SPS-ST) in Matlab/Simscape Power Systems. A dedicated Matlab script is developed for simulating three IEEE standard benchmarks. Thousands of contingencies, such as line faults, generator losses, and load switches, are simulated to generate the database. During each simulation, twelve pieces of information are recorded to facilitate the implementation of artificial intelligence-based relay algorithms and the identification of early catastrophic indicators of the power systems stability. Furthermore, this database allows to modernize and develop the new protections functions. The load-flow convergence and dynamic systems response serve as criteria for verifying the correctness of implementation. The IEEE 39, 68 and 145 test systems with solar photovoltaic power plant (WECC PV) integration can be used to generate extensive training and testing databases simultaneously. The model is available in Matlab-Central file exchange platform, facilitating power systems training, research, and development endeavors.

articleTitle: A Resilience Management Method for Power Outages with Dynamic Prioritization of Consumer Resources
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: To address power outages, cooperative utilization of consumer-side resources through power sharing and exchange is expected to enhance resilience. In our previous study, we proposed the multilevel resource priority management method that considers the use of individual resources and incorporates load suppression. Building on this foundation, this study proposes an extended resilience management method that dynamically prioritizes consumer resources based on the state of consumer resilience. In this method, the tradeoff between consumer priority and mutual-support priority is defined as a multistage dynamical priority management model and formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming optimization problem. As a numerical example, the simulation of a consumer model with 512 households representing the size of one feeder in a distribution system was conducted. Furthermore, an equality index was introduced to assess variations in resilience services between each consumer. Consequently, the relationship between the priority management model, cooperative group size, and equality index was clarified.

articleTitle: Impact of Commissioning a Static Var Compensator at the Loma Plata Substation
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the impact of commissioning a Static VAR Compensator (SVC) at the electrical substation in Loma Plata, a city in the Chaco region of Paraguay. The study examines the electrical characteristics of the station and the localities it serves. The research analyzes steady-state and transient conditions after commissioning the SVC, showing improved load margin at the substation bus and a rapid compensator response to contingency events.

articleTitle: Temporal Hierarchy Reconciliation Network for PV Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) stations are distributed spatially and their power forecasts play an important role in coordinated decision-making in power systems. For different decision-making requirements, power forecasts at various temporal scales are investigated. However, these forecasts are implemented independently. In this paper, we consider the inherent relation among these power forecasts at various temporal scales and propose a Temporal Hierarchy Reconciliation Network (THReN). THReN adopts a temporal hierarchical structure to generate coherent multi-site forecasts for various temporal scales. It integrates base forecasts and reconciliation processes in a trainable architecture that effectively captures both intra-level spatio-temporal correlations and inter-level temporal dependencies for a set of distributed PV stations. With a temporal hierarchy matrix S, THReN ensures prediction coherence while enhancing forecasting accuracy at multiple scales. Experiments on a synthetic dataset demonstrate that THReN consistently outperforms other competing methods.

articleTitle: RT-DETR-E: A Real-Time Model for Foreign Object Detection in UAV Inspection Power Lines
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, drone technology is gradually used by the power system inspection, especially in the inspection of power lines to detect foreign objects. Since UAVs can't fly for long time imitating lines due to the influence of hardware equipment, and the photos of foreign objects after shooting are usually small and medium targets, it is difficult to recognize them using the traditional YOLO network. To address this problem, this paper proposes an improved model RT-DETR-E based on RT-DETR; for the problem of background noise interference in the dataset, Concat_CAA and BFBE are designed to enhance the feature extraction capability and lightweight design of the model; for the problem of low inference speed of real-time detection, the real-time detection effect is achieved by introducing DySample. The experiments show that RT-DETR-E is optimal in mAP50 and params compared with some classical models of YOLO and RT-DETR series in the public dataset. Compared with the baseline model, the detection accuracy is improved by 3.4% and the number of parameters is reduced by 4.2%, which demonstrates the excellent performance and potential of RT-DETR-E in real-time detection. Moreover, the RT-DETR-E proposed in this paper reaches 140.8 (frames per second) in terms of inference speed, which meets the demand of real-time UAV detection.

articleTitle: A Study on a Charge and Discharge Control Method of Multiple Storage Batteries Utilizing Machine Learning for Voltage Control in Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Due to the secondary use of battery storages installed in electric vehicles, it is expected that the installation of battery storages on consumer sides will increase significantly in the future. When storage batteries and photovoltaic power generation are used together, reverse power flows to distribution grids may affect voltage rises of distribution grids. In this study, we will report on the charge and discharge control method that utilizes Q-learning to suppress the influence on the distribution grids as much as possible, assuming that the consumers will autonomously and decentrally control the charge and discharge of storage batteries. We evaluated the applicability to multiple storage battery charge and discharge control when PV output changes are assumed in the power distribution system. We confirmed that adding a function to maintain the output of the storage batteries to avoid their repeated recharging operation is more effective in controlling the voltage of the storage batteries within an appropriate range. We also evaluated that the system is applicable to the case where the PV output pattern is varied.

articleTitle: Dynamic Time Warping Technique for Condition Monitoring of High Voltage Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The reliability of high voltage circuit breakers (HVCBs) is crucial for power grid operation. Therefore, it is vital to monitor the condition of HV CBs accurately. One of the online condition monitoring measurements for HVCBs is the trip/close coil current measurement which is straightforward to implement. This paper presents a novel application of dynamic time warping (DTW) to compare healthy and defective trip/close coil current signals, facilitating the detection of defects in HVCB operation. DTW is used to assess the temporal variations between different signal patterns, providing a robust comparison even under varying operational conditions. An experimental HVCB setup is used to validate the proposed method, showcasing its capability to detect different types of faults in the coil mechanism.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Energy Management System for Smart Buildings
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The requirement for efficient and sustainable urban environments has made energy management in smart buildings a crucial topic of research and development in recent years. This study targets gaps in energy management research by dynamically choosing the best ventilation devices (AC, fans, windows) based on the changeable environmental factors like temperature, humidity, and wind speed using reinforcement learning thus elevating energy management in smart buildings. The ML model was trained via reinforcement learning (RL), with a fuzzy control scoring system designed to take the consequent user satisfaction and power cost of the device selected by the model based on the weather conditions (temperature, humidity, and wind speed), to grade the selection during training. Moreover, verification of the model's decision-making mechanism was executed by an integrated simulation platform through case studies showing their applicability in typical and extreme conditions. The proposed system proved the capability of understanding the weather state to select the optimal device to turn on for the lowest power cost and highest user satisfaction in the building. This supports the United Nations (UN) sustainable development goals (SDGs) by promoting sustainable, cost-efficient energy use and improved living standards.

articleTitle: Health Prognosis of Lithium-Ion Batteries using CNN-SVR Fusion Model for Dynamic Discharge
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The state of health (SoH) estimation of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) plays a pivotal role in safe and reliable operation of an electric vehicle (EV). Numerous methods have been proposed in the recent times for LIB's SoH diagnostics and prognostics. The accuracy in terminal voltage estimation during charging and discharging is equally crucial to extract the health indicators (HIs) required for the SoH estimation. However, in practical driving scenario, LIB charges and discharges dynamically resulting in incomplete capture of voltage curve details. Therefore, this paper proposes an SoH estimation framework depending on terminal voltage extraction based fusion model. Firstly, the discharge terminal voltage is reconstructed based on importance sampling to obtain voltage-time (V-t) curve for batteries operating under variable temperatures. Secondly, the HIs related to SoH are extracted and their co-relation with SoH is analyzed. Furthermore, a fusion model based on convolutional neural network (CNN) and support vector regression (SVR) is established.
