The results show that the performance evaluation indicators of the proposed framework are superior as compared to SVR and CNN alone, with root mean square error (RMSE) of less than 0.00416 and mean absolute error (MAE) less than 0.00315 for all batteries.

articleTitle: Impact of Installing Lightning Arresters on Low Voltage Networks in Areas with High Lightning Incidence Per Kilometer
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The concession area of Sociedad Eléctrica del Sur Oeste S.A. (SEAL) faces a significant challenge due to the high incidence of atmospheric discharges, ranging from 12 to 30 lightning strikes per square kilometer annually. These discharges result in critical failures in transformers and electrical networks. Current medium-voltage protections are insufficient to effectively mitigate electrical surges that damage secondary windings, leading to increased maintenance costs, service interruptions, and reduced system reliability. The presented article addressed these shortcomings through the implementation of Surge Protective Devices (SPDs), a technology already validated in Europe and Brazil. In critical areas such as Chuquibamba, Valle del Colca, Chococo, Orcopampa, and Huancarama, 1,300 SPDs were installed, distributed across three-phase and single-phase networks. The results demonstrated a significant reduction in failures, preservation of transformers, and low implementation costs-approximately $89.22 per three-phase SED and $44.61 per single-phase SED-totaling an investment of $28,119.00, which significantly reduces losses caused by the problem. Financial analysis confirmed the project's profitability, with an Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 14.9%, a Net Present Value (NPV) of $61,298.84, and a payback period of seven years. This viable and effective model reinforces the company's commitment to innovation and energy efficiency, setting a precedent for expansion into other critical areas.

Author Keywords: Cost-Effective Solutions y High Lightning Incidence Areas

articleTitle: An Adaptive Class Topper Optimization for Scheduling Thermal Generation with Cubic Fuel Cost Function
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a population-based metaheuristic optimization algorithm, i.e., an adaptive class topper optimization (ACTO), for solving cubic fuel cost objective functions economic load dispatch with equality and inequality constraints. The working principle of the proposed methodology is based on the learning improvement of students in a class for knowledge updating. In general, the use of polynomials function to represent generator fuel cost curves in real-time economic dispatch is an industry standard, and it significantly impacts the accuracy of the economic load dispatch solution. Many existing conventional methods struggle to deal with cubic fuel cost functions that reflect the non-linearity of the real generator response. Therefore, the proposed optimization technique is particularly efficient in solving non-linear higher-order objective functions for both smaller and larger generating units and it significantly decreases the computational time to obtain optimal fuel cost. The proposed algorithm has been successfully tested on the following dispatch case studies: 3 units, 26 units cubic fuel cost function without losses and 3 units cubic system with losses for different loading conditions. The results reveal that the adaptive class topper optimization algorithm outperform other existing methodology when addressing the higher-order generator cost functions.

articleTitle: Comparative Impact Analysis of Factors Affecting Renewable Energy Integrated and Conventional Energy Sources in Smart Grids Using MATPOWER
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Integrating renewable energy sources (RES) alongside conventional energy sources (NRES) in the grid has introduced challenges that highlight the need for a detailed analysis of various performance factors. Factors such as active and reactive power losses, voltage deviation, transmission line loading, power factor, fast voltage stability index, and capacity factor require careful evaluation to understand their impact on grid performance. In this study, MATPOWER's optimization tools are used to model both NRES and a combined NRES + RES setup. The analysis compares the performance of each configuration a cross these factors. Findings indicate that integrating RES with NRES generally enhances performance across most of the analyzed factors compared to using NRES alone. The insights from this study offer valuable guidance for grid operators and policymakers, aiding in the balanced integration of RES with NRES to optimize smart grid performance and resilience.

articleTitle: Development of Composited Indices for Congestion Management in Low Voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for managing congestion and voltage unbalance in the distribution network through the development of a composited indices that integrate thermal violation and voltage violation indices with the voltage unbalance factor. The composite indices identify and rank congestion points by combining multiple factors. The unbalance problem is investigated based on the integration of photovoltaic system and electric vehicles in low voltage network. In addition, this approach serves as a strategic guide for deploying battery energy storage systems, effectively reducing thermal and voltage violations while enhancing network stability and flexibility.

articleTitle: Effects of Sea-Bed Undulation and Front-Wall Geometry on the Performance of a Bottom-Seated OWC Device
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Oscillating water column (OWC) is a type of wave energy converter (WEC) device that extracts the ocean water energy by harnessing the periodic motion of the water waves and the subsequent pressure difference at the air water interface. The main advantages of such devices are their efficiency even at low wave frequencies, scope for hybridization with other systems like solar and wind energy converters, cost effectiveness and minimum to no negative impact on the environment. This study is based on a bottom-seated OWC device on an undulated seabed. Here, the effect of sea-bed undulation is studied for different geometrical configurations of the front wall of the OWC device to attain optimum hydrodynamic performance. Previous studies have neglected the effects of seabed undulation which generally occurs for real oceans. This physical problem is converted into a boundary value problem (BVP) under the linearized water wave theory and potential flow theory, which is then solved using the boundary element method (BEM). It has been found that numerical method like BEM provides better and more accurate solutions when the domain geometry is more complex as compared to analytical methods, which can't handle the complex domains. Physical parameters such as the slope of the front wall, the width of the chamber, and the bottom undulation are considered for the present investigation to obtain the optimized configuration for maximum power generation.

articleTitle: Economic Analysis of Typical Models of Renewable Hydrogen Production via Electrolysis
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Renewable hydrogen production via electrolysis is rapidly advancing but faces challenges such as high operating costs, renewable energy volatility, immature storage and transportation technologies, and limited market demand. The economic viability of these projects depends heavily on business models that reduce costs and enhance competitiveness. This paper proposes five typical business models for renewable hydrogen production via electrolysis and conducts empirical studies on their economic viability. The results show that grid-connected projects are currently more economically viable than off-grid projects, with some grid-connected (total amount controlled) models showing slightly better economic performance than hybrid (total amount controlled) models.

articleTitle: An Agent-Based Model of Microgrids with Distributed Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy sources poses a challenge to stability of power systems, particularly microgrids, which are more vulnerable due to their small capacity and low inertia. To address instability, system components and their interactions need to be represented to more efficiently understand and optimize complex systems. Agent-based modeling enables autonomous operation and collaborative interaction, making the system adaptable to changes efficiently, making it ideal for microgrid management. In this paper, an agent-based microgrid simulation model is proposed. By independently representing microgrid components such as generators, energy storage systems (ESS), loads, environments and controllers, models can dynamically simulate the behavior of power systems, respond to system changes in real time. To validate the proposed model, experiments are conducted based on IEEE 13 bus system, and the results show that with the use of ESS, the frequency peak is reduced from over 62 Hz to around 60 Hz. In the case of sudden demand fluctuations, the frequency remains relatively stable, staying close to 60 Hz. The model demonstrates flexibility and robustness in managing renewable energy fluctuations and sudden load changes.

articleTitle: An Aumann-Shapley Approach to Allocate Capacity Deferral Benefit Among Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: High penetration of distributed energy resources provide power system planners with a practical substitute to high cost reinforcement plans. Locating DERs near load centers and optimizing their power dispatch, can reduce the utilization of power system assets resulting in the deferral of investments. To incentivize DERs to provide desired dispatch, it is essential to quantify their individual contribution towards capacity deferral benefits. This paper introduces an Aumann Shapley based allocation scheme that distrubutes deferral benefit among various DERs. The scheme is analytically validated against key fairness axioms desired by the DER stakeholders. A series of case studies on IEEE European distribution network are conducted to assess its fairness attributes. The results demonstrate that the proposed allocation scheme satisfies the desired fairness standards and also provides locational signal for future DER installations.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Void Growth in Electrical Solder Material
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper deals with the void growth in electrical materials such as Sn-Ag-Cu solder for the electronic packaging. The small-sized Sn-Ag-Cu strip with a notch is analyzed using the finite element method. Under the electric load, the electromigration, thermo-migration, stress-migration and pure atomic diffusion are the driving forces for the void growth. As a result, the electro-thermo-structural-diffusion coupled-field are obtained. Due to the atomic migration, the void growth history is obtained using the element-birth-and-death simulation in ANSYS software. Furthermore, the electric resistance and time to failure of the Sn-Ag-Cu solder strip are determined for the electronic reliability and design.

articleTitle: Improvements of a SI-Engine Generator to Use Bioethanol and Bioethanol-Water Blends
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The research aims to study the performance and emission of a SI-engine generator, fueled with bioethanol and bioethanol mixed with water up to 30% compared with gasohol 91. This engine generator was tested with increasing main-jet diameters and compression ratios at 3,000 rpm and different loads. After adjusting for these factors, the engine performance with these fuels was found to be at its peak at 2.82 kW. The use of bioethanol and bioethanol mixed with water up to 30% was lower engine performance than gasohol 91. Bioethanol was higher carbon dioxide (CO2) and carbon monoxide (CO) emissions but bioethanol mixed with water up to 30% was lower CO2, CO, and nitrogen oxide (NO) emissions than gasohol 91. Outstandingly, bioethanol mixed with 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> water was more engine performance and less CO2 and NO emissions than gasohol 91 and bioethanol.

articleTitle: A New Electronic Voltage Transformer Applicable to AMI Smart Meters
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Voltage transformers (VTs) used in the distribution-level smart meters in advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) systems are mainly composed of iron cores and windings, and are insulated with epoxy resin. Therefore, they are bulky and heavy. In addition, the complex winding structure easily leads to uneven epoxy resin grouting, so partial discharge may occur between layers in VTs, which may eventually lead to explosion accidents. This study proposes a new electronic voltage transformer (EVT), whose secondary voltage output not only meets the accuracy required by the AMI smart meter but also needs to be used to provide the power required by the AMI smart meter. The new EVT is based on the principle of resistive voltage dividers. Moreover, a push-pull power amplifier is combined to realize high power output and impedance matching. Besides, the new EVT adopts a modular design. For different distribution voltage applications, the voltage measurement requirements of 380 V/114 V, 11.4 kV/114 V or 22.8 kV/114 V can be realized by changing the cascade module. The experimental results show that the new EVT for the 380 V/114 V application not only successfully drives the AMI smart meter, but also meets the Class 0.1 according to IEC standard 60044–7.

articleTitle: Quantum Algorithms for Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This paper explores the use of quantum computing, specifically the use of HHL and VQLS algorithms, to solve optimal power flow problem in electrical grids. We investigate the effectiveness of these quantum algorithms in comparison to classical methods. The simulation results presented here which substantially improve the results in [1] indicate that quantum approaches yield similar solutions and optimal costs compared to classical methods, suggesting the potential use case of quantum computing for power system optimization.

articleTitle: A Novel Study on Suppressing Sodium Dendrites Using Coatings for Separator Based on the Piezoelectric Principle
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Currently, sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) have a wider temperature adaptability than lithium-ion batteries, but they still perform poorly in cold weather, especially below -20°C. In such conditions, the mobility of sodium ions decreases, leading to higher internal resistance, which negatively impacts charge-discharge efficiency and battery capacity. This work introduces a novel SIBs separator consisting of a separator and a coating made from polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF). This coating is applied to conventional battery separators and uses its piezoelectric properties to create mechanical stress, preventing the formation and growth of sodium dendrites during charge-discharge cycles. Further experimental results indicate that without the nanofiber piezoelectric coating, sodium-ion batteries short-circuit after fewer than 50 cycles at a current density of 0.2 mA due to dendrite formation. However, with the coating, the batteries can exceed 240 cycles, significantly extending their lifespan. This technology has effectively addressed the problem of battery short circuits resulting from the growth of sodium dendrites and is expected to promote the wider application of SIBs technology.

articleTitle: Effect of Various Parameters on Hot Spot Heating Power of Parallel Cell Cluster Type PV Module
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The authors have previously proposed a parallel cell cluster method as a method to reduce hot spot heating power in Si monocrystalline solar cells. In the proposed parallel cell cluster method, the conventional series connected cell group are divided into equal parts and configured in parallel, so that and the heating power is reduced by lowering the voltage of the normal cell group. Since factors such as solar intensity, shadow ratio, and defect resistance vary depending on the situation, it is necessary to consider the effect of these parameters on the heating power. Therefore, this paper compares how the heating power varies depending on various parameters in the proposed method with the conventional method. As a result, the proposed method showed a higher reduction in heating power compared to the conventional method, and under the conditions with the highest reduction effect, the heating power was approximately 0.92 [%] of that of the conventional method.

articleTitle: Multi-Timescale Distribution Network Optimization Based on Deep Transfer Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: With the development of the power grid to the direction of intelligence and digitization, distributed generations have gradually become an important part of the distribution network. However, the randomness of distributed generations' output influenced by surrounding environment, together with the high-dimensional distribution network scheduling model, brings great challenges to the formulation and implementation of distribution network scheduling optimization. Therefore, this paper proposes multi-timescale distribution network optimization based on deep transfer reinforcement learning. Firstly, considering difference of devices' action speed, the coordination of the discrete device and the continuous device is realized through cooperation between different timescale. Therefore, action plan for discrete device is determined by stochastic optimization in the day-ahead phase. Secondly, a deep reinforcement learning optimization model of continuous devices is established in intraday phase and trained according to short term prediction data to lay the model foundation for knowledge transfer. Then, the trained model is used to do parameter transfer. In this way, the scheduling strategy can be adjusted according to the real-time output data, so as to ensure a more stable and optimized operation of the distribution network. The experimental results show that the proposed method can adjust the scheduling strategy quickly, the algorithm is more convergent, and the exploration is faster.

articleTitle: Challenges and Methodological Innovations in Developing a Digital Twin for Photovoltaic Inverters
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study examines the complexities associated with developing a digital twin (DT) for photovoltaic (PV) inverters and presents a systematic strategy for addressing these challenges. It highlights the significant impact of digital twin modeling on improving maintenance approaches for PV systems by enabling predictive maintenance and early anomaly identification. In addition, the paper addresses the challenges encountered in implementing a digital twin for photovoltaic inverters, including the complexity of the data and systems involved, as well as the need for accurate real-time analysis. The proposed methodological framework addresses these challenges by integrating robust data management systems, model validation techniques and integration strategies to ensure accurate correlation between the digital twin and the performance of the physical inverter. This methodology aims to improve the reliability and functional efficiency of photovoltaic inverters in the context of extended renewable energy systems. Furthermore, this paper provides researchers and academics with a concise overview of the different approaches to the digital twin of photovoltaic inverters, presenting an in-depth analysis of its complexities, challenges and potential impact on the progress of inverter research.

articleTitle: The Electrothermal Characteristics Under Short-Circuit Stress in Planar Gate SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: The third-generation wide-bandgap semiconductor, silicon carbide metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (SiC MOSFET), has emerged as a focal point in the industry, particularly concerning its robustness under short-circuit conditions. This study presents experimental validations and simulation analyses of the short-circuit failure mechanism, along with the behavior of silicon carbide planar gate power MOSFETs under short-circuit stress. A prevalent phenomenon observed in the short-circuit failures of numerous SiC power devices is the positive feedback of current due to thermal runaway, which typically manifests as an inability to effectively suppress the drain current of the SiC MOSFET after the gate voltage is turned off. In planar gate structures, this phenomenon represents the principal cause of short-circuit failure. Moreover, the degradation of the gate oxide subjected to short-circuit stress can also lead to short-circuit failure of the gate-source, constituting an additional factor. Building upon this foundation, practical tests were conducted on the VDMOS devices to validate the results of the simulation analysis, and a theoretical examination was performed to elucidate the actual failure mechanisms involved. Investigating the short-circuit stability of these devices yields critical insights for the application of power components.

articleTitle: Electrical Design Review Based on BIM-MEP Model
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study proposes an electrical review method for mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) using Building Information Modeling (BIM). The purpose is to reliably simplify the review work, directly evaluate electrical equipment and wiring layout, and calculate short-circuit current and line voltage drop based on BIM-MEP models. MIEtech Company did the study in collaboration with Taiwan Power Company (TPC), the unit responsible for reviewing the design of electrical appliances. This study aims to simplify the review process, reduce manual review errors, and improve the timeliness and reliability of reviews. In addition, the review system provides insight into the process and correctness of the precise integration of wiring, plumbing, and electrical equipment into the building structure, improving the safety and reliability of building electricity. In addition, it can also assist electrical engineers in using BIM to enhance the accuracy and self-detection capabilities of circuit design and improve the timeliness of the design process. Finally, the educational training for the review unit was performed and demonstrated using Autodesk Revit and bimU with the operating system Windows 11 (virtual machine).

articleTitle: Advancing EVA/SiC Hybrid Nanocomposite Encapsulation for Performance Optimization in Concentrated Solar Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Encapsulant materials play a crucial role in regulating silicon wafer temperatures, bonding PV cell layers, and mitigating thermal stresses. The incorporation of nanoparticles into an ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) copolymer matrix presents a promising strategy for improving photovoltaic (PV) performance. In this study, silicon carbide (SiC) nanoparticles were integrated into the EVA matrix at concentrations of 10%, 20%, and 30% through a solvent casting technique to form a hybrid composite. Characterization techniques, including FT-IR spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and thermo-gravimetric analysis (TGA), confirmed the uniform dispersion of SiC nanoparticles, ensuring the stability and enhanced properties of the composite. The 30% SiC loading exhibited the most favorable thermal and physical characteristics. A three-dimensional conjugate heat transfer model was developed to simulate fluid flow within a conventional heatsink, coupled with the CPV layers containing the hybrid encapsulant's properties. Two flow configurations-parallel flow (PF) and counter-flow (CF)-were investigated under a solar concentration ratio (CR) of 15 suns. Results indicated that the hybrid encapsulant layer improved both average and local silicon layer temperatures by approximately 8%, with the CF configuration showing superior thermal performance. Electrical efficiency reached 19%, exceeding typical literature values for polycrystalline solar cells, which report about 15% efficiency. The model predicted that the CF configuration provided more uniform temperature distribution, whereas PF exhibited non-uniform temperature variation across the cell surface.

articleTitle: A Game-Theoretical Analysis of Retired Electric Vehicle Batteries in Energy Storage Markets
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study adopts a game-theoretical approach to examine the impact of introducing retired electrical battery-based (REVB-based) energy storage systems on the energy storage market and the electrical grid. A bi-level Nash-Stackelberg game is formulated with three players: power stations (PSs), energy storage aggregators (ESAs), and energy storage service operators (ESSOs). In this framework, power stations participate in the day-ahead market and develop bidding strategies for electricity supply. Energy storage service operators, equipped with either standard storage systems or REVB-based systems, determine optimal bidding strategies for charging and discharging power. These strategies aim to provide load-shaving during peak-load periods and enhance the integration of solar power during base-load periods. The standard and REVB-based energy storage systems differ in their maximum charging-discharging cycles, investment and maintenance costs. The ESA acts as an intermediary between the day-ahead market and the energy storage market, aggregating the charging and discharging power from ESSOs. Specifically, during peak-load periods, the ESA arbitrages between the two markets by selling stored discharging power purchased from ESSOs to the day-ahead market. Conversely, during base-load periods, the ESA purchases charging power from the day-ahead market to charge energy storage systems and purchases charging capacity from ESSOs to facilitate the accommodation of renewable energy. The ESA is regarded as the leader in the Stackelberg-Nash game, with PSs and ESSOs acting as the followers. Additionally, incentive compensation is considered to address potential profit losses incurred by the ESA during baseload periods. Numerical simulations are conducted to explore how the introduction of REVB-based energy storage systems influences profits and system performance within the energy storage and day-ahead markets.

articleTitle: Integrating Autonomous Electric Vehicle Charging Stations in Local Energy Communities
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Autonomous electric vehicles (AEVs) represent a transformative technology that must be carefully considered in the design of modern energy management systems. Addressing the challenges associated with AEVs and their charging infras-tructure while leveraging the opportunities they present is crucial. In this study, we propose the integration of inductive AEV charging stations into multiple local energy communities, treating these stations as community members. To ensure fair benefit allocation, we employ a game-theoretic approach. Three operational scenarios are analyzed based on the available resources at the charging stations: (1) no photovoltaic (PV) generation or battery energy storage systems, (2) PV generation without storage, and (3) a combination of PV and battery storage systems. Charging station pricing is determined by the added value of integrating into the community energy model. The results highlight the potential of this approach to enhance decentralized energy ecosystems, promoting fairness and sustainability across all stakeholders.

articleTitle: Research on the Propagation Mechanism of Fault Components in Distribution Networks and Its Impact on Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: When a fault occurs in a distribution network, the propagation of fault components can affect the power quality of non-fault lines, leading to deviations in voltage, voltage fluctuations, imbalance, and harmonic content, all of which may exceed the standard limits. Reports of abnormal operation of non-fault load lines due to fault component propagation are common, with phenomena of propagation across different voltage levels also observed. To address the challenge of quantitatively evaluating fault component propagation in distribution networks, this paper proposes models for the propagation of steady-state and transient fault components under various fault conditions, and the effectiveness of these models is validated through simulation. The results show that, in the case of low-voltage distribution faults, not only will non-faulted loads on the same busbar be impacted by power quality degradation, but high-voltage distribution lines may also be affected to varying degrees.

articleTitle: Low Carbon Charging Schedule of Electric Buses: Case Study in Denmark and Japan
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study examines regional differences in time-varying carbon dioxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{CO}_{2})$</tex> emissions from power systems in Denmark and Japan, influencing on the low-carbon charging schedules of electric buses in public transportation systems. The time-varying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> emissions differ significantly due to variations in the penetration rates of variable renewable energy (VREs) sources, particularly wind power. Numerical experiments reveal that under an optimal charging schedule, total <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> emissions in Denmark are 81% lower in summer and 71% in winter compared to Japan when chargers are available only at their depot. Additionally, distributing chargers across all bus terminals ensures the feasibility of transportation in winter. Furthermore, distributed chargers at bus terminals have potential to reduce emissions by up to 4% further by expanding the flexibility of charging times to align with VRE utilization throughout the day. This international comparison highlights the critical importance of optimizing charging schedules in high VRE penetration systems, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> emissions exhibit significant daily fluctuations.

articleTitle: Multi-Location and Multi-Feature LMP Forecasting: A 2D Spatiotemporal LSTM-CNN Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Accurate Locational Marginal Price (LMP) forecasting is crucial for effective energy procurement in electricity markets, as it helps utilities make informed, cost-efficient decisions. This study addresses the limitations of traditional models by introducing a 2D spatiotemporal LSTM-CNN model that utilizes multi-location and multi-feature inputs to improve forecast accuracy specifically for Batangas I Electric Cooperative, Inc. (BATELEC I). Using the Dynamic Interval Price Collection (DIPC) dataset from the Independent Electricity Market Operator of the Philippines (IEMOP), which provides 5-minute interval data from June 2021 to August 2024, the model captures short-term price fluctuations across resource locations. Results indicate that the 2D Multi-Features and Multi-Locations LSTM-CNN model outperforms 1D and 3D configurations, achieving the lowest RMSE of 5.0976E-03 and effectively capturing spatial and temporal dependencies. These findings support improved decision-making in electricity markets, with future applications in real-time adaptive forecasting for enhanced market responsiveness.

articleTitle: Optimal BESS Scheduling with Real-Time Assessment for Time-of-Use Customers Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: This study presents an optimal day-ahead operational scheduling strategy for a battery energy storage system(BESS) to achieve savings for a time-of-use(TOU) customer. This optimization problem is solved using a Particle Swarm Optimization(PSO) algorithm with an evaluation of its sensitivity to photovoltaic(PV) and load forecast errors. A new initialization process based on two non-optimized algorithms is proposed to enhance PSO convergence during the optimal scheduling process. By charging the BESS with surplus PV generation or during off-peak periods and discharging it during peak times or when contracted demand limits are exceeded, an initial particle population is provided as an input to the PSO. The state of charge(SOC) is maintained within the normal range by stopping the BESS output selected by the PSO as needed. The PSO's performance is assessed in real-time operation using historical PV and load data. The proposed method is simulated using MATLAB software to verify its effectiveness showing 17% and 10% cost saving over one day and one month, respectively. Additionally, the PSO demonstrates robust performance for forecast error under 10%.

articleTitle: Electrical Load Forecasting Using LSTM for Power Stability
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Accurate electric load forecasting is essential for effective energy management and optimization. This project leverages Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, a type of recurrent neural network (RNN), to predict electric load due to their ability to capture long-term dependencies in time series data. The dataset used for this study was sourced from Kaggle, provided by a power supply company in Johor, Malaysia, with weather data (including temperature and humidity) collected from Weather Underground. The model is trained using electric load data along with additional features such as time, temperature, and humidity. Model performance is evaluated using several metrics: Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Mean Squared Error (MSE). The discussion will examine how modifications to the data, model architecture, the training and validation process impact the forecasting results. Results are compared across three different LSTM architectures: 1-layer, 2-layer, and 3-layer models. The best resulted obtained with a MAPE of 16.33%. These findings may assist the utility company in optimizing electricity generation and power supply stability, planning equipment maintenance, and resource procurement. Future work will focus on enhancing model accuracy to ensure more reliable predictions.

articleTitle: Decentralized Distributed Online Multiagent Systems Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2025 15th International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE)
abstract: Paper suggests a distributed online structure recognition-based summation model predictive control approach for the frequency management. The benefit of the suggested scheme is fundamentally adjustable to the varying system status. As the distributed system global and local variables are recognized via online estimation, the system is robust against exotic system agitation. Paper is employing a split-KalmanNet filter that synchronous the states of recognized model, facilitating a plug and play. The controller is using the recognizing enlargement incremental model, which merges optimal summation performance to reduce the frequency steady state errors. Also, quadratic optimized controller produces constraints restriction to the control inputs not beyond limits during faults, in which supporting controller in executing frequency ride through. The suggested scheme is proved via the IEEE 123 bus regarding the communication delay. Simulation results show enhancement of transient performance, in contrast to the PI.

abstract: It is with great enthusiasm that we present the proceedings of the International Conference on Power, Energy, and Electrical Engineering (CPEEE). This conference brings together leading researchers, engineers, academics, and industry professionals from across the globe to share their latest findings, innovations, and insights in the fields of power systems, energy technologies, and electrical engineering. The papers compiled in this volume represent the cutting-edge research and collaborative efforts that are shaping the future of these critical disciplines.
